root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening apart, creating an interval, and widening or spreading.
root_idea.development: From this spatial principle come the broad pass or road between mountains, bodily and object-related separation, cleaving, and rounded internal space. The lexicon also records divergent branches involving unripe material, rapid movement, and excessive talk.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun/adjective is a distinct, Quran-attested lexical item and is displayed under the normalized citation form فَجّ.

senses.definition: A broad mountain pass or road; a wide route through or between mountains.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the plural فِجَاجًا denotes broad passes or wide roads, including routes through mountainous terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the feet or legs wide apart, or to part them widely; to straddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals. The straddling posture may be adopted for urination; the expression is also used of a female camel or sheep or goat in connection with milking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opening or interval made between two things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general spatial expression underlying more specific uses such as parting the legs widely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bow, to have its string set far from the part where it is grasped or from its central belly; a bow in that condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related passive and adjectival forms describe the same configuration of the bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave or plough the earth in a disapproved manner; ground cleft in that way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ground-related usage is associated with ploughing or an objectionable cleaving of the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse and similar animal, to intend or desire to run.
To make a thing crude or insufficiently cooked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative preparation or cooking usage.
A lexical noun for the melon identified in the source as the type called Indian by Persians.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unripe or insufficiently matured; of food, insufficiently cooked, and of a wound, not matured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to fruit and other melons, and to things that should have ripened or cooked more fully.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an ostrich, to become mute or silent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is reported of either sex of the ostrich.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel a road of the kind called فَجّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person travelling along such a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten, go quickly, or be quick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of a person or, more broadly, of a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opening or intervening space between two mountains.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal form for a mountain opening, distinct from the Quranic فَجّ road or pass.
A plural form; the singular is not supplied in the cited evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male ostrich said to lay one egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported zoological term, distinct from the homonymous plural associated with roads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stem of the raceme of a palm tree.
Excessive, frivolous, boastful, clamorous, or disorderly talking; a person characterized by such talk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application describes a palm tree that promises abundant fruit but fails to fulfill the promise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A valley, especially a wide valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the dialect of some people of Yemen it may denote a narrow, deep valley; elsewhere it can be applied more generally to a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A solid, hard hoof rounded like a cupola.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Such a hoof is described as well-formed or approved.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Wide separation of feet, knees, or hocks.
Widely parting the legs and the general opening-between-things usage.
Desiring to run, said of a horse and similar animal.
Making a thing crude or insufficiently cooked.
Broad road or pass between mountains.
Unripe or insufficiently matured fruit and related things.
Infinitive-noun pointer to an already represented entry.
State of being unripe or insufficiently cooked.
Loquacity, babbling, clamour, and disorderly talk.
Loquacious or boastful person and figurative palm-tree use.
Person with legs wide apart or straddling.
Bow with string distant from its central part.

cautions: Lane's lexical material is indexed under the contracted root ف ج, while the canonical QAC root is ف ج ج; the Classical evidence has therefore been aligned through the supplied geminate-contraction match.
The Quranic form is tagged by QAC as both noun and adjective; the three occurrences are presented under one lexical sense rather than split by grammatical tagging.
